title: MemGraphRAG: Memory-based Multi-Agent System for Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation

problem.claim: Traditional RAG struggles with large-scale, unstructured corpora containing highly fragmented information, while existing GraphRAG methods can produce inconsistent, conflicting, and fragmented graphs.

gap.claim: Existing GraphRAG graph construction lacks a global perspective over the whole corpus.

contributions.claim: MemGraphRAG introduces a memory-based multi-agent framework for high-quality graph construction.
The framework uses collaborative agents with shared memory to maintain unified global context, resolve logical conflicts, and preserve structural connectivity during extraction.
The paper proposes a memory-aware hierarchical retrieval algorithm for the constructed graph.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present MemGraphRAG as a novel framework introducing a memory-based multi-agent system.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on multiple benchmarks reportedly show that MemGraphRAG outperforms state-of-the-art baseline models with comparable efficiency.

narrative_sequence.summary: RAG uses external knowledge to mitigate hallucinations in large language models.
Traditional RAG has difficulty with large, fragmented, unstructured corpora.
GraphRAG captures structural relationships, but existing methods construct graphs from isolated fragments without a corpus-wide perspective.
The resulting graphs may be thematically inconsistent, logically conflicting, and structurally fragmented, harming retrieval.
MemGraphRAG combines shared-memory multi-agent graph construction with memory-aware hierarchical retrieval and is reported to outperform state-of-the-art baselines at comparable efficiency.

source_observation.claim: Fragment-level graph extraction can produce inconsistent, conflicting, and disconnected graph structures.

interpretation.claim: Corpus-wide context may be important for maintaining consistency and connectivity during knowledge-graph construction.

application.claim: For large fragmented corpora, provide shared global memory or another corpus-level context during extraction and retrieval.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether global memory is necessary for all corpora or query types.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the benchmarks, datasets, metrics, baselines, or numerical results.
The abstract does not specify the multi-agent architecture, memory implementation, conflict-resolution procedure, or retrieval algorithm details.
The abstract does not quantify the meaning of comparable efficiency.
